title: Basic nutrition and food-safety rules from WHO, Codex and Sphere guidance
jurisdiction: Global default; replace with national rules where they exist

rules.audience: adults; scale down for children by energy needs
rules.message: Sodium above 2 g per person per day (5 g salt).
rules.source: WHO, Healthy diet fact sheet; WHO sodium intake guideline (2012)
WHO guideline: sugars intake for adults and children (2015)
WHO guideline: saturated fatty acid and trans-fatty acid intake (2023)
WHO guideline: saturated fatty acid and trans-fatty acid intake (2023)

rules.message: Less than 400 g of fruit and vegetables per person per day.

rules.audience: adults, assuming about 2.5 meals a day
rules.message: A single meal uses more than about 40 % of the daily sodium limit.
rules.source: Derived from the 2 g/day WHO limit (program choice)

rules.audience: general food distribution when it is people's main source of food
rules.message: Below 2,100 kcal per person per day.
rules.source: Sphere Handbook (2018), food security and nutrition standards
WHO Five Keys to Safer Food (key 4)
WHO Five Keys to Safer Food (key 4)

rules.message: Frozen food warmer than −18 °C (block if thawed).
rules.source: Codex code of practice for quick frozen foods (CXC 8-1976)

rules.message: Cooked food left out of temperature control for more than 2 hours.
rules.source: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food (key 4)
Codex general standard for the labelling of prepackaged foods (CXS 1-1985)

rules.message: Past best-before: quality, not safety; local law decides whether it may be donated.
Allergens not declared: do not serve to people with known allergies; relabel or discard.

disclaimer: DRAFT. Derived from public guidance; not reviewed by the source bodies (WHO, FAO/WHO Codex Alimentarius Commission, Sphere). Values are simplified for planning and checking; they are not medical advice, do not cover therapeutic or infant feeding, and must be reviewed by qualified nutrition and food-safety staff before use.
